requirement: Parse access-log lines into typed records with a compiled named-group pattern that must match the whole line, treat a dash size as zero, count malformed lines while skipping blank ones, and list paths of 5xx responses.
skeleton: Compiled LINE pattern and TIMESTAMP format, frozen Request dataclass, parse_line using fullmatch, scan collecting requests and a malformed count, and server_errors filtering on status.
caption: Log parsing with the standard-library re module and named groups. A module-level compiled LINE pattern captures ip as four dotted groups of up to three digits, ts inside square brackets, a quoted method limited to GET, HEAD, POST, PUT and PATCH followed by a path, a three-digit status and a size that is digits or a dash. parse_line(line) strips the line and uses fullmatch, so trailing text or an unknown method makes it raise ValueError naming the malformed log line. It reads the groups by name, turns a dash size into 0, parses the timestamp with datetime.strptime and the TIMESTAMP format including the UTC offset, and returns a frozen, slotted Request dataclass with integer status and size. scan(lines) skips blank lines entirely, appends each parsed request and counts lines that raise ValueError, returning the list and the count. server_errors(requests) returns the paths whose status is 500 or higher. The fixture asserts the fields and the timezone-aware timestamp of a GET line, that a HEAD line with a dash size has size 0, that trailing text and a BREW method raise ValueError, that scanning a blank line, a good line, garbage and spaces yields one request and one malformed line, and that statuses 499, 500 and 503 give two server errors.

plan.intent: Turn access-log lines into typed records
constraints: The pattern must match the entire line or ValueError is raised
Only GET, HEAD, POST, PUT and PATCH methods are accepted
A dash size means zero bytes
Blank lines are skipped and malformed lines are counted
Server errors are statuses of 500 and above

rationale.teaches: A compiled pattern with named groups read by name, fullmatch for whole-line validation, and typed conversion of captured text.
rationale.why: Regex parsers that use match instead of fullmatch or loose alternations accept junk, and special tokens like a dash size break integer conversion, so each edge needs its own crafted line.

ops.docstring: Parse access-log lines with a compiled regular expression and named groups.

ops.source:
LINE = re.compile(
    r"(?P<ip>\d{1,3}(?:\.\d{1,3}){3}) "
    r"\[(?P<ts>[^\]]+)\] "
    r'"(?P<method>GET|HEAD|POST|PUT|PATCH) (?P<path>\S+)" '
    r"(?P<status>\d{3}) (?P<size>\d+|-)"
)

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Request:
    """One parsed access-log entry."""

    ip: str
    ts: datetime
    method: str
    path: str
    status: int
    size: int

def parse_line(line: str) -> Request:
    """Parse one whole line, rejecting anything the pattern does not fully match."""
    match = LINE.fullmatch(line.strip())
    if match is None:
        raise ValueError(f"malformed log line: {line!r}")
    size = 0 if match["size"] == "-" else int(match["size"])
    return Request(
        ip=match["ip"],
        ts=datetime.strptime(match["ts"], TIMESTAMP),
        method=match["method"],
        path=match["path"],
        status=int(match["status"]),
        size=size,
    )

candidates.why_wrong: match anchors only at the start, so lines with trailing text are accepted.
A dash size becomes -1 instead of 0.
Status 500 itself is not counted as a server error.
Any word is accepted as a method, so BREW lines parse.
Blank lines are parsed and counted as malformed.
